text:
maria: Quick hit 90 mins.0We need a compact policy for fast onboards that balances customer speed vs platform stability. Draft idea below.
dave: send it.
maria: Proposal A (fast-path): 1 perf smoke (P95 < baseline + 20%), 1 automated quality sweep (n=100), 5% canary for 72h, telemetry hooks + explicit opt-in by requesting customer. If any critical trigger -> immediate rollback.
lina: sounds workable. we should define 'critical trigger' specifically. also, how do we surface canary traffic customers in Console?
ryan: +1. propose triggers: error-rate >0.5% (1h avg), quality-regression >4% on core prompts (rolling 6h), memory OOMs >=1 in 24h. If trigger hit, system should mark model as provisional-failed and cut canary to 0%.
maria: agree. add a short rule for noisy signals: require 3 consecutive eval windows before auto-unpin to avoid flapping.
dave: operationally, i want a command we can run to force-unpin with a reason, e.g. `/catalog unpin 1758001111 --reason "quality drop"`. ops + oncall must get notified.
ryan: add to that: when unpin happens, create a migration ticket template and DM the owning PM.
lina: also add a 'rollback safety net' where if a pinned model is unpinned by auto-rollback, we create an automatic read-only snapshot of the model metadata and customer mappings for investigations.
maria: good. on contractual surface: fast-path must be excluded from Dedicated uptime SLAs and must be toggled as "trial pin" in contracts. sales ok with that?
dave: sales asked for an escape hatch: customers can buy "pinned-stability" addon that guarantees we won't place them on fast-path without explicit consent and gives migration assistance.
ryan: implementation notes: the catalog database needs fields: pin_state, canary_fraction, canary_start, canary_origins (list), rollback_count. catalog-bot: Note: schema change ticket created #CAT-412.
lina: telemetry: show these panels in Console: canary health (errors, latency delta), quality drift, affected customers list, token-cost delta. set alert thresholds to paging for errors and warning for quality.
maria: onboarding checklist (fast-path): - smoke perf test (script `./bench/smoke.sh`) - quality N=100 automated - model card + compatibility notes - legal privacy check done - opt-in form filled by customer.
dave: include a short code snippet for the rollback rule in RFC so engs can implement quickly: ```yaml
rollback_triggers:
  - name: quality_regression
    threshold_percent: 4
    window_hours: 6
  - name: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 0.5
    window_hours: 1
  - name: memory_oom
    occurrences: 1
    window_hours: 24
```
ryan: also publish a migration playbook template: tokenizer shim steps, embedding-dim compatibility check, and recommended eval prompts. put in docs at https://redwood.docs/migrations/fast-path-playbook
lina: timeline: pilot with 3 community models this sprint, product + infra signoff, then enable feature-flag for pilot accounts.
maria: owners: product=dave, infra=ryan, eng=lina, legal handled by me. i'll draft RFC and include the yaml snippet and checklist.
dave: one more thing: deprecation windows for pinned models that move off a catalog version? propose minimum 60 days for general customers, 150 days for enterprise with paid migration.
ryan: agree but add 'emergency retire' clause for security/fatal regressions with 24h notice.
maria: wrap-up: i'll create RFC and tag reviewers. anyone want to add risk items?
lina: mention risk: canary traffic could leak training artifacts if not isolated. ensure data exfil controls on canary path.
dave: +1. thanks team. :thumbsup:
catalog-bot: Feature flag `catalog.fast_path_enabled` created for Product team. Toggle in Console -> Feature Flags.
